section.sectionSummaryBrief: There are two types of contemplation leading to humility: one focusing on one's lowliness and distance, and another focusing on the purpose of the descent being for an ascent, as explained by the Mitteler Rebbe and the Tzemach Tzedek.
section.t: And this is the explanation:
Now, regarding the contemplation that brings about submission and lowliness,
there are two ways.
In the aforementioned discourse of the Mitteler Rebbe,
it is explained
that to arrive at submission and lowliness is through contemplating one's extreme lowliness and great distance, etc.,
and that the contemplation should be with a good and precise accounting, called "Marei d'Chushbana" (masters of accounting).
[And it can be said
that this statement—that the contemplation must be with a good and precise accounting—is in the manner explained at length in Shaar HaYichud,
that when the contemplation is general,
one's comprehension of the matter is only in the aspect of makif (encompassing),
and he can also deceive himself.
And in order for him to have a true and internal comprehension, it is through contemplation in a detailed manner.
However, after contemplating the details, one must examine and contemplate the general.
[And it states there,
that thus he received from his father
(the Alter Rebbe)
from the Maggid, with a complete explanation].
And it can be said
that this statement—that the contemplation must be with a good and precise accounting—means that he should contemplate the details.
For in addition to the fact that an accounting
(in general)
is an accounting of details,
a precise accounting is one where he is exacting in every detail].
And in the aforementioned discourse of the Tzemach Tzedek, he adds,
that the matter of "Marei d'Chushbana" is in the manner of our Sages' statement
on the verse,
"Bo'u Cheshbon" (Come, let us account),
"Come and let us calculate the accounting of the world."
The accounting of the ultimate purpose of the descent of the creation of the world and the purpose of the descent of his soul into this world,
that the descent is for the sake of an ascent.
And when he contemplates that he is not fulfilling the intention for which his soul descended below,
he will come to lowliness.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The difference between the two types of lowliness is that one is a preparation for prayer due to the virtue of self-nullification, while the other is itself connected to prayer because it contains the feeling of G-d's exaltedness.
section.t: And the distinction between the two matters is,
that according to the explanation that lowliness
(the heaviness of head before prayer)
is through contemplating one's extreme lowliness and great distance,
this lowliness
(heaviness of head)
is a preparation for prayer,
because through self-nullification one reaches the most exalted levels,
for "whoever humbles himself, the Holy One, blessed be He, raises him up."
And according to the explanation that lowliness is through contemplating that the purpose of the descent is for the sake of an ascent,
this lowliness is a preparation for prayer
(not only because of the virtue of self-nullification,
but also)
because the matter of this lowliness itself is related to prayer.
For in order for the descent to be felt by him
(and that the intention of the descent is for the sake of an ascent)
it is through the feeling of the exaltedness and wondrousness of G-dliness.
And the more he feels the exaltedness of G-dliness, the more he will feel the greatness of the descent.
And since his lowliness stems from his not having fulfilled the purpose of the descent,
therefore, in his lowliness, some of the exaltedness of G-dliness is felt.
And to note from what the Alter Rebbe wrote in his Shulchan Aruch,
that before prayer one must think of the exaltedness of the blessed G-d and the lowliness of man,
it can be said
that the thought of man's lowliness is not an independent matter but a continuation and result of the thought of G-d's exaltedness.
And based on this,
that the heaviness of head is a preparation for prayer is not only because of the virtue of self-nullification, but also because in the heaviness of head, the exaltedness of G-d is felt,
the matter of prayer.
However, the contemplation of G-d's exaltedness is in relation to man's lowliness,
and therefore,
through this contemplation he comes to submission and lowliness.
And the contemplation during prayer is of G-d's exaltedness itself,
and the self-nullification that comes through this contemplation is
(not submission and lowliness,
but rather)
being included in G-dliness
(as above, section 9).

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The distinction between pre-prayer and in-prayer contemplation also lies in the nature of G-d's exaltedness itself, where prayer's contemplation reaches the Ein Sof beyond relation to worlds, leading to a love that desires only Him.
section.t: A)
And to add,
that the distinction between the contemplation before prayer and the contemplation during prayer is also in the matter of G-d's exaltedness itself.
For this self-nullification in prayer is that he becomes completely nullified
(similar to the offering that was burned in the supernal fire),
the nullification of the essence of the soul
(as brought above in section 9 from the Baal Shem Tov),
this is,
because the contemplation of prayer
(the Shema)
is in the Ein Sof, which is above any connection to worlds,
for "everything before Him is considered as nothing,"
the contemplation
of "Hashem is One."
And the Rebbe Maharash explains,
that the matter
(aspect)
of "One" is like "You are
One and not in number."
And he explains,
that regarding matters that are in relation to each other
(except that one is greater and more elevated than the other)
the matter of accounting applies, in the quantity and quality of the superiority of one over the other.
And like Atzilus and BY"A,
between which there is some relation
[for although there is a partition (Parsa) between Atzilus and BY"A,

nevertheless, the bringing into being of Chochmah of Beriah from Chochmah of Atzilus is through the Chochmah of Atzilus itself clothing itself in the Parsa and causing the bringing into being of Chochmah of Beriah],
therefore,
an accounting applies regarding the greatness of the superiority of Atzilus over BY"A.
But regarding the Ein Sof, for whom all worlds
(even the world of Atzilus)
are incomparable to Him
[and their bringing into being is through the tzimtzum,
for the matter of tzimtzum is the concealment of the light],
the matter of accounting does not apply there,
"You are One and not in number."
And through this contemplation he will come to the love of "Who
is for me in heaven, and with You I desire nothing on earth,"
that he will have no desire for the lower Garden of Eden
(earth)
nor for the upper Garden of Eden
(heaven)
but only for Him alone.
And in the manner of the Alter Rebbe's statement,
"I want absolutely nothing; I do not want Your Garden of Eden, I do not want Your World to Come, etc.; I want nothing more than You alone."
